candidates.name: Hypopharyngeal cancer
support_spans: a left pyriform fossa mass was seen invading and compressing the left hemilarynx
MRI of the neck demonstrated a large necrotic mass centred on the left pyriform fossa
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a tumor in the hypopharynx.

candidates.name: Laryngeal cancer
support_spans: the larynx was fixed, the airway significantly narrowed but no stridor was present
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings suggest involvement of the larynx.

candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: a poorly differentiated malignant tumour on rapid onsite evaluation
candidates.why: The patient's tumor is likely a squamous cell carcinoma, given the location and presentation.

candidates.name: Metastatic cancer
support_spans: focal uptake with sclerotic changes in the left femoral neck, suggesting bony metastasis
candidates.why: The patient has evidence of metastatic disease, suggesting a malignant tumor with metastatic potential.

candidates.name: Hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: FDG PET–CT confirmed high metabolic activity in the hypopharyngeal mass
candidates.why: The patient's diagnosis can be confirmed with a biopsy or imaging studies, such as PET-CT.

candidates.name: Poorly differentiated carcinoma
support_spans: ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of the left neck mass and right level II lymph node showed a poorly differentiated malignant tumour on rapid onsite evaluation
candidates.why: The patient's diagnosis can be confirmed with a biopsy or fine-needle aspiration.
